$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.14,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.14/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 7eece2c00f44d1812c881a1f0741297e3a9f9a6b43b94e0f9136f6d9ef49ed12 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.14/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
7eece2c00f44d1812c881a1f0741297e3a9f9a6b43b94e0f9136f6d9ef49ed12 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
